items.title: Antonelli seals the title after a near-retirement run to the Mexico podium
items.summary: Kimi Antonelli secured his first Drivers' Championship with third place in Mexico and became Formula 1's youngest champion. Mercedes later revealed that the car returned with oil under the floor and a cracked sump; Antonelli said the engine began to struggle about four laps from the end. He finished on 380 points, ahead of Max Verstappen on 261 and Lewis Hamilton on 259.
items.why_it_matters: The Drivers' title is settled, but the constructors' championship remains live: Mercedes leads Ferrari 630–504.

items.title: Verstappen takes a sixth Mexico City win
items.summary: Max Verstappen won from fifth on the grid, finishing 0.799 seconds ahead of Hamilton for his third victory of 2026 and sixth at the Mexico City Grand Prix. Hamilton finished second and Leclerc fourth after his five-second penalty.
items.why_it_matters: The updated results show the order after all post-race decisions, not the provisional order at the chequered flag.

items.title: Post-race penalties reshaped the points-paying order
items.summary: Piastri received a ten-second penalty for his collision with Lindblad. Gasly was given a stop-and-go for failing to slow in a double-yellow sector, while Colapinto received ten seconds for not slowing sufficiently under a single yellow. The latest official classification places Piastri 13th and scoreless; the initial report had him 15th before the later Alpine decisions.
items.why_it_matters: Keep the updated final classification distinct from the intermediate post-race report; the Alpine rulings also removed both drivers from the points.

items.title: Vasseur confirms talks with Hamilton and Leclerc after Mexico battle
items.summary: After Leclerc's five-second penalty for gaining an advantage in the opening-lap battle with Hamilton, Fred Vasseur confirmed that he met with both drivers before the Brazil weekend. He said Ferrari comes first and that he expects them to act professionally, but would keep the discussion private and was not asking them to be best friends.
items.why_it_matters: The penalty and subsequent management response are confirmed, but the private conversation does not establish a new team-order policy.

items.title: Mexico's red flag changed the strategy picture
items.summary: The post-qualifying Pirelli chart compared a fastest Medium-to-Soft one-stop on laps 35–41 with a Soft–Medium–Soft two-stop at laps 19–25 and 45–51; average pit loss was 22 seconds over 71 laps. In the race, Verstappen went from Medium to Soft on lap 27 and changed to another Soft under the red flag. Antonelli kept his opening Soft stint to lap 43 before switching to Medium, then also used Soft after the red flag. Pirelli said one stop would otherwise have been the most competitive option.
items.why_it_matters: The published windows were pre-race simulations, not actual stint timing; neutralisations changed the strategies that decided the result.
